newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Head of Bulgaria foreign investment agency resigns.
newsitem.headline: Head of Bulgaria foreign investment agency resigns.

text.p: The director of Bulgaria's foreign investment agency Daniela Bobeva said on Friday she had tendered her resignation over disagreements with the latest amendments to the foreign investment law adopted by parliament.
"I am resigning as I could not convince parliament to adopt a foreign investment law with fewer restrictions," Bobeva told Reuters.
On Thursday parliament passed amendments to the foreign investment law extending tax benefits to foreign investors in a bid to speed up privatisation.

Under the amendments no Value Added Tax, customs duties and other taxes will be levied on non-fiscal foreign investments like machines and equipment, patent rights, licences, trademarks, technologies and know-how.

However, parliament introduced a minumum $50,000 foreign investment registration threshold, under which 6,801 smaller joint-venture companies will not be eligible to repatriate profit and other investment incentives, said Bobeva.
Also parliament did not revise an earlier ruling under which foreigners are banned from land ownership, which restricts foreign investment in agriculture, said Bobeva.
She also criticised a ban on licensing foreign insurance companies to operate in the country. Foreign insurers may only operate as joint ventures with Bulgarian insurers.
Foreign investments will be given preferential treatment up to 10 years after their registration in Bulgaria irrespective of possible legislative curbs that might come into force during that period.

Bulgaria has the lowest level of foreign investment among its ex-communist neighbours. The Balkan country of 8.4 million people has attracted around $800 million in investments from abroad since 1990.
